svg.title: The kitchen maths. Scaling: per serving amounts scale three ways. Linear for staples like rice and chicken. Sub linear, servings to the power 0.65, for oil, pastes and herbs, so 10 servings need about 4.5 times one serving, not 10 times. Fixed for spices: you buy one pack of garam masala whether you cook for two or ten. Unit conversion includes per piece weights, so 2 onions can come from a 1 kg pack. Product ranking in matcher.ts adds points for ingredient key match, how much of the ingredient label the product name says back, rating and popularity, and subtracts for pack waste, extra packs and cost. The budget ladder: first swap to cheaper packs, then drop optional ingredients, then explain the shortfall in plain language.

section.h2: Cooking for ten is not ten times the oil

div.div: Multiple of one serving, by head count

ul.li: Sub linear (servings to the 0.65): oil, pastes, herbs
Fixed: one pack of masala for 2 or 10

div.div: Each candidate is scored per ingredient in matcher.ts

ul.li: ▲Carries the ingredient key (closest key ranks highest)
▲Its name says the ingredient label back
